human_tolerance.notes: Wikipedia notes that it nests in structures such as roofs and begs for human food at the wildlife-urban interface. ADW (CC BY-NC-SA) reports that it is abundant in campgrounds where it takes human handouts.

phases.name: caching
phases.note: Caches food near the burrow, especially during late summer and fall (Wikipedia).

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: Hibernates over winter in a burrow (Wikipedia). ADW gives hibernation starting late August to November and ending late March to May, depending on elevation; a single window cannot express that, so the temperature triggers switch the state and this window is an authored compromise.

vocalizations.description: A squeak, or a growl, given when it feels threatened. Wikipedia says the species is generally not very vocal.

taxonomy.note: Sciuridae, Callospermophilus, (Say, 1823). GBIF match confirmed at species rank and ACCEPTED on 2026-11-01.

external.note: GBIF usage key 7593288. iNaturalist taxon 180010 (species, active) matched on 2026-11-01. ITIS TSN 76772 from Wikidata P685.

common_names.note: Common name from the iNaturalist preferred common name, which the issue also uses.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 IUCN category Least Concern (Q211005).

range.note: Wikipedia: native to western North America; distributed in the Rocky Mountains of British Columbia and Alberta, and through much of the western United States. Country-level codes only.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walk, trot and gallop are the modes the host animates. Climb is omitted: no permissive source states that the species climbs, and the quadruped body plan has no climb pose.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Wikipedia: hibernates, with gains in body weight before hibernation (endotherm).

traits.nest_type.note: Wikipedia: it lives in and makes burrows and hibernation dens (up to 100 feet long but typically shallow). Nesting in structures such as roofs is also recorded.

traits.perching.note: Not a perching animal: a ground-living burrower with no perching behaviour in the sources.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg 0.257: at least 0.05 kg and under 1 kg, so Small.

traits.mass_kg.note: Wikipedia gives adult weight 120 to 394 g and no mean. 0.257 kg is the midpoint of that range, derived by calculation. ADW (CC BY-NC-SA) gives the same range (120 to 394 g).

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Wikipedia: adult weight 120 to 394 grams, converted from grams.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia gives 23 to 29 cm. 0.26 m is the midpoint, derived. ADW (CC BY-NC-SA) gives 235 to 295 mm.

traits.lifespan_y.note: LOW CONFIDENCE, non-commercial last resort. ADW states an average of 7 years in the wild, attributed to Bartels and Thompson (1993), and says the figure likely excludes juvenile mortality, so it may overstate a typical lifespan. Wikipedia (CC BY-SA) gives only 'up to about seven years', which is maximum-style wording. AnAge's text is the same: 'appear to live up to 7 years'; a captive maximum of 10.4 years is not used.

traits.diet.note: Authored allocation from Wikipedia's food list: pine nuts and acorns (mast), herbs and shrubs (browse and graze), insects (invertebrate), eggs, young birds and lizards (vertebrate), and carrion. No quantitative diet data found in open sources. Fungi and human foods are not allocated. Seed is kept small because the list names nuts and seeds under mast.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia: most adults are independent, reside alone in burrows and compete for resources, but may assemble at sites with abundant food. group_size [1, 2] is authored from that description.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Non-commercial last resort. ADW: 'Golden-mantled ground squirrels are mostly diurnal, but can be active at any time during the summer.' Wikipedia does not state a time of day.

traits.defense.note: Judgement. Wikipedia says it becomes vocal when threatened and that it darts away from predators in the wider sources; flight is the authored main response.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement, midpoint. Campground animals take handouts (ADW), but the species is alarm-calling and flees from predators (Wikipedia).

habitat.use.note: Authored split from the Wikipedia habitat description: forests, chaparral, meadow margins and sagebrush, with rocks or forest litter for shelter. Mostly ground-living.

habitat.resources.note: Authored weights from the Wikipedia food list and cache description: mast in late summer and fall, insects in spring and summer, leaf litter as cover.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia: nests in structures such as roofs and begs for human food at the wildlife-urban interface. ADW (CC BY-NC-SA) notes campground abundance and handouts.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: hibernates over the winter, and gains weight in summer beforehand.

seasonal.triggers.note: Authored temperature thresholds, judgement. Neither Wikipedia nor ADW gives temperatures. Entry at 5 C for 14 days and exit at 8 C for 7 days are chosen to fit a late-autumn entry and spring emergence.

seasonal.phases.note: Caching in late summer and fall: Wikipedia. Dormancy: Wikipedia says it hibernates over winter; ADW gives hibernation starting late August to November and ending late March to May, depending on elevation. The 10-01 to 04-30 window is authored from those ranges and is an approximation.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Judgement: juveniles are smaller than adults. ADW says juveniles resemble adults by 40 days of age, which is not used here.

behavior.note: Species-local FSM expresses the documented omnivorous food list with distinct mast and invertebrate feeding actions. Invertebrate feeding uses April through July and a 0.35 choice in August and September when insects are near. The mast resource calendar is August through November, while the October through April winter gate preempts its October and November entries; mast feeding is effectively enabled in August and September. Winter shelter rest uses the existing 10-01 through 04-30 dormancy approximation; daytime surface actions are gated by is_day and night forces shelter rest. A close threat overrides the rest gates. These are broad US-calendar modelling choices because hibernation varies by elevation; the FSM has no regional or temperature-persistence memory.

vocalizations.alarm_squeak.note: Wikipedia: it makes squeaking noises or growls when it feels threatened, and is generally not a very vocal species. Timing and cooldown are authored.

look.note: Authored block-mesh look for the previewer. Colours follow the Wikipedia description: grey-brown body, tawny to reddish mantle over the shoulders (the neck part), pale underparts, a white stripe down each side of the back (the back_stripes part, without the black borders), and no facial stripes. Proportions are judgement.
